summary: Smokies lookout on Rich Mountain near Cades Cove; the register lists it removed, and cement foundation blocks remain on the summit spur.

facts.status_note: Tennessee's register lists the tower as removed. Only cement foundation blocks are described at the summit.

access.note: Reached on foot from Rich Mountain Road, which is closed in winter.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. A small spur trail near Cerulean Knob leads to the summit, where the old foundation blocks are.

evidence.supports: Register: Rich Mountain at 3,699 ft in Blount County, park code gsmnp, marked removed
evidence.quote: Rich Mountain 3699' Blount FB2634 gsmnp removed

evidence.supports: The gsmnp park code is the GSMNP landforms legend on the register page
Trailhead on Rich Mountain Road, 2.2 miles from the Cades Cove Loop Road
evidence.quote: The trailhead is located on the Rich Mountain Road, 2.2 miles from the Cades Cove Loop Road.

evidence.supports: Rich Mountain Road is closed in winter
evidence.quote: Rich Mountain Road is closed in the winter.

evidence.supports: Spur trail leads to the highest point on Rich Mountain, after Cerulean Knob
evidence.quote: arriving at Cerulean Knob, where a small spur trail leads to the highest point on Rich Mountain

evidence.supports: Cement foundation blocks of the old fire tower remain at the spur end
evidence.quote: In the small opening, cement blocks that were once the foundation of the old Rich Mountain Fire Tower remain.

evidence.supports: The park's fire towers were abandoned in the 1970s
evidence.quote: In the 1970s, fire management techniques and approaches to fire patrol changed, and the fire towers in GRSM were abandoned.

evidence.supports: All but four towers and one cabin were removed from the park in the following decade
evidence.quote: Over the next decade, all but four of the towers and one of the cabins were removed from the park.

evidence.supports: The park is Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM)
evidence.quote: When the Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM) was established in 1931

evidence.supports: All but four of the park's towers have been dismantled and removed
evidence.quote: Now all but four have been dismantled and removed

evidence.supports: Surviving towers Mount Cammerer, Mount Sterling and Shuckstack can still be climbed
evidence.quote: Of those, three can still be climbed by hikers seeking to enjoy magnificent long-range views: Mount Cammerer, Mount Sterling and Shuckstack Mountain.

evidence.supports: The fourth survivor is the Cove Mountain tower
evidence.quote: The exception is the Cove Mountain tower

evidence.supports: A different Rich Mountain near Hot Springs, NC, has a standing lookout
evidence.quote: Right out of the popular trail town of Hot Springs, the AT takes you almost up to a standing lookout on Rich Mountain.

evidence.supports: That Hot Springs lookout is listed as standing

sources.title: Every Day Is Fire Day: A Study of Historic Fire Towers and Lookout Life in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park

notes_for_editor: No source gives this tower's build date, builder or removal date, so the story has no built section. The Hiking Project guide gives no elevation or year; it is matched to the tnlandforms Blount entry by name, Smokies location and summit. The Clemson thesis PDF returned HTTP 403, so only its abstract was read. A 1934 photo caption in the Southern Appalachian Digital Collection (sadc.qi-cms.com/omeka/items/show/66551) appeared in search but timed out twice and is not used. A park cultural-resources record would supply the dates.
